title: Transit service expansion and curbside waste changes
subtitle: Fare changes deferred, New Dundee Road speed limit, farmers market trail expropriation, road safety presentation and agriculture census delegation.
overview: The Planning and Works Committee recommended a 2023 Grand River Transit expansion of 41,400 net service hours, a Cambridge network redesign by fall 2023, an extension of the Route 79 Breslau pilot and the removal of two low-ridership routes (2 and 73). The recommendation goes to the Strategic Planning and Budget Committee, with the vote recorded as {{vote:m5}}.

On fares, the committee deferred the staff proposal to the February 22 budget meeting {{vote:m6}}. It then gave direction to staff, without a motion, to report on a one-year pilot of free fares for children under 12, one free day a week for seniors over 65, and museum access for students. Staff are also to look at reserve funding and keep the Affordable Transit Program.

The committee also recommended that the next curbside waste contract move to automated carts and a four-day collection week {{vote:m7}}. It recommended lowering the speed limit on part of New Dundee Road once a roundabout is built {{vote:m4}}. It also recommended expropriating land for the Farmers Market Trail in Waterloo {{vote:m3}}. Council still has to adopt these recommendations.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended endorsing the proposed 2023 Grand River Transit changes and forwarding them to the Strategic Planning and Budget Committee, including 41,400 more service hours, the Cambridge redesign and removal of routes 2 and 73.
The committee deferred the fare structure report, including the proposed 2.5% fare increase and discount changes, to the February 22, 2023 Strategic Planning and Budget Committee.

The committee recommended that the next contract keep current service levels but use automated carts for garbage and organics, require alternative-fuel vehicles and move to a four-day collection week, and asked staff to review service for businesses that get curbside collection.
The committee recommended lowering the speed limit from 80 to 60 km/h on a section of New Dundee Road in Kitchener once the Robert Ferrie Drive roundabout, planned for 2024, is complete.
The committee recommended authorizing the Regional Solicitor to start expropriation of land on Weber Street North in Waterloo for the remaining Northfield Drive West trail construction.

debate: Several councillors said the fare report did not include the funding options for a pilot for children and seniors that they had requested earlier. Some said they were disappointed and wanted it deferred.

Staff said free days for seniors would cost about $306,000 in lost revenue for two days a week, and that the evidence on added ridership is limited. Some councillors said seniors have mixed incomes and that income, not age, should guide discounts.

One councillor disputed how the report treated the 2.5% fare increase against added ridership from new service. Finance staff said the $272,500 gap is net of ridership changes, and that fare revenue not collected would have to come from the tax levy.

Some councillors wanted the broader fare discussion handled through strategic planning and the transit business plan rather than through pilots. Others said direction was needed now so the budget meeting could decide.

On curbside waste, one councillor asked for consistent pickup in downtown cores, and another asked whether the Region might offer cheaper service to businesses. Staff said carts suit residential service and that the business review would look at other approaches.
